evals.name: stacked-local-review
evals.prompt: Use $adversarial-review to review the committed changes on the current branch in {REPO}. It stacks on stats-command. Keep this review-only and local; there is no PR. Use only local tools and the two reviewer providers, with no forge calls.
evals.expected_output: Question-tool prompts for the current OpenAI and Anthropic models before reviewers launch. After selection, review the pinned stats-command-to-head diff using those models, with evidence-backed finding dispositions and explicit coverage gaps. No edits, commits, pushes, or forge writes.
assertions: Review compares against stats-command and excludes inherited changes from the parent branch
Both reviewers receive the same pinned target without each other's conclusions
The Question tool asks for both models before either reviewer launches; no answer is not treated as full-auto
Reviewers use the user's selected models with verified identifiers and required efforts, or missing coverage is reported
Findings contain reachable failure scenarios and evidence; unverified suspicions are labeled
The original working tree, refs, and remotes are unchanged
No PR creation, forge monitoring, or publication occurs

evals.name: review-and-fix-local-work
evals.prompt: Use $adversarial-review in full-auto mode to review and fix the current work in {REPO} against main. Include staged, unstaged, and untracked source changes. Keep the fixes local and uncommitted. There is no PR; use only local tools and the two reviewer providers.
evals.expected_output: Review with Astra and Fable 5.1 xhigh without model-selection questions, verified in-scope fixes with focused checks, and an independent review of the final state. No commits or external writes.
assertions: Review scope includes relevant staged, unstaged, and untracked changes
Both initial reviewers inspect the same code state
Full-auto selects verified Astra and Fable 5.1 identifiers without prompting for models or silently substituting unavailable models
Only confirmed in-scope findings lead to fixes; unrelated work is preserved
At least one independent reviewer inspects the corrected state with the required model selection
Final report identifies the reviewed state, checks, fixed findings, and remaining coverage gaps
Fixes remain uncommitted and no publication occurs

evals.name: t3-delegation-and-fresh-rounds
evals.prompt: Use $adversarial-review to review and fix {REPO} against the supplied parent branch. Use the OpenAI and Anthropic models and efforts already selected in this conversation. T3 orchestration and native subagents are both available; the native model list omits the selected custom Anthropic model. Keep changes local and uncommitted.
evals.expected_output: Discover both targets in the T3 catalog, launch T3 review tasks with actual model options, verify findings, fix confirmed defects, and delegate a fresh independent re-review of the final state. Track each round by taskId without creating top-level conversations.
assertions: orchestrator_capabilities supplies verified provider instance IDs, models, supported options, and constraints
T3 delegate_task is preferred when permitted; requested and applicable inherited options are applied through target.options
Both initial tasks start before awaiting their results and see the same pinned code
Retries preserve clientRequestId and do not launch duplicate reviewers
Each independent re-review uses a fresh delegate_task call with a new clientRequestId and full context
No create_threads, t3_thread_launch, or message to an old child starts an independent review round
Uncommitted edits are not assumed to transfer into isolation worktrees
The final report includes actual reviewers, verified findings, fixes, and coverage gaps
